prompt_text: I need a dental implant in Charlotte. Which specific dental practices should I call, and why?
q1_prompt_text: Who is the best dentist in Charlotte for a dental implant?
answer_verbatim:
I can do that — I just need one quick detail so I give you accurate, local names and numbers: what ZIP code or neighborhood in Charlotte do you want the implant done near? Also tell me if you prefer a specialist (oral surgeon or periodontist) vs a general dentist who places implants, and whether cost/insurance or sedation options are important.

While you reply, here’s how I’ll proceed and what to call (so you get the best results):

Which types of practices to call (and why)
- Oral & Maxillofacial Surgery practice — best for surgical complexity (impacted teeth, bone grafts, sinus lifts, IV sedation). Call these if you expect extractions, heavy grafting, or advanced sedation.
- Periodontist office — specialists in gums, bone grafting and implant placement; great for single/multiple implants with strong focus on long-term soft-tissue outcomes.
- Prosthodontist or restorative dentist experienced with implants — best for planning and placing the final crown and ensuring proper bite/esthetic function; important if you want a single clinician to restore the implant.
- Multidisciplinary implant center — coordinated teams (surgeon + restorative dentist) for full-mouth or complex cases.
- Dental school clinic — lower cost and supervised care (e.g., UNC Adams School of Dentistry in Chapel Hill) if price is a major factor.

Key reasons to pick practices:
- Board-certified specialists (oral surgeons or periodontists) for complex work
- On-site CBCT 3D imaging for accurate planning
- Experience with the implant brand/type you want (Nobel, Straumann, Zimmer, etc.) and a clear restorative plan
- Transparent pricing, financing, and written treatment timeline
- Good before/after photos and patient reviews, and clear warranty/maintenance policy

Questions to ask when you call (script you can use)
- “Hi, I’m interested in a dental implant. Do you place implants here or refer out?”  
- “Who places the implants — a periodontist, oral surgeon, or general dentist? Are they board certified?”  
- “Do you have on-site 3D (CBCT) imaging?”  
- “How many implants does this provider place per month/year?”  
- “Will the surgeon do bone grafting or sinus lifts if needed?”  
- “What implant systems/brands do you use?”  
- “Do you handle the crown/restoration here, or will another dentist do that?”  
- “Do you offer sedation (oral/IV) and what are the costs?”  
- “Do you provide a written estimate, timelines, and financing options?”  
- “Can I see before/after photos and patient references or reviews?”

What to look for in their answers (red flags vs. green flags)
- Green flags: board certification or fellowship training; on-site CBCT; clear restorative plan; written estimate and timeline; many positive recent reviews; before/after photos.
- Red flags: vague answers about who does the restoration; no imaging available; push to do everything in one visit without evaluation; unwillingness to provide a written plan/estimate; very low price with no explanation.

If you give me your ZIP code/neighborhood and any preferences (insurance, sedation, budget), I’ll list 5–7 specific practices in Charlotte to call, with short reasons to call each and what questions to ask them.
